conviction_note: The date is confirmed. The issuer's own 2026-10-01 notice says about 17:00 ET on 7 October, with the call at 10:00 ET on 8 October, so the whole reaction falls inside the scored window. That is a change from Richelieu's usual mid-morning release; the change in timing carries no information by itself and is not filed. The two measurements agree in sign. The findings sum to -1.70: a sell-side bar of EPS 0.46-0.48 that needs about +40-50bp of year-on-year margin expansion, against two quarters of disclosed 20-30bp tariff dilution, plus a likely walk-back of the 'close to 11%' full-year margin target. The scaled number is -0.72 (p_up 42 on an abs move of 4.5) because the bar comes from aggregator sites built on two analysts, consensus was already trimmed from 0.51 to 0.48, the stock is down 11.5% YTD and holds near its range low, and the revenue line looks in line once the FX tailwind is counted.

EPS 0.46 / revenue 538.66M from WealthAwesome (https://wealthawesome.com/will-richelieu-hardware-ltd-rch-beat-earnings-estimates-in-its-next-report-10062026-earnings, 2026-10-06, 2 analysts). EPS 0.48 (range 0.47-0.49) / revenue 532.77M from Yahoo Finance and Investing.com, per search snippet only, because the Yahoo analysis page failed to render (https://www.investing.com/equities/richelieu-hardware-ltd.-earnings); the snippet says Yahoo's trend shows the estimate was 0.51 a week earlier. My build is EPS about 0.44-0.46 and revenue about 529-536M, so revenue is roughly 0% against the bar.
positioning_check: CIRO consolidated short position via TMX (baseline, business date 2026-10-06): 1,127,095 shares, 2.24% of shares, 13.97 days to cover over 30 days. The high days to cover reflects thin turnover (about C$2.4M a day), not a crowded short. No change series exists. There is no listed option on the Montreal Exchange, so there is no skew or option lean. Analysts: 2, both hold, average target C$38.75 (+9.6%), after both cut targets on 2026-07-13 (41 to 38 and 42 to 39, per MarketBeat https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/TSE/RCH/forecast/). Tape: -1.73% over 20 days, -4.09% over 5 days, -1.92% intraday on the seal day. The baseline's priced_lean_pct of +1.53 comes almost entirely from the short_squeeze prior, which I do not regard as meaningful at 2.24% short.

findings.finding: The sell-side bar of EPS 0.46-0.48 (+7-12% on 0.43) needs a Q3 EBITDA margin of roughly 11.8-12.0% against 11.4% a year ago. Richelieu's own disclosures show tariff pass-through diluting margin 20-30bp a year (Q1 9.3% vs 9.6%, Q2 10.6% vs 10.8%), and the CFO said on 2026-07-09 that there is 'nothing else' structurally. On revenue of about C$534M and a margin of 11.1-11.3%, EPS comes out at about 0.44-0.45, a miss of about 5%. Consensus has missed in 3 of the last 4 quarters by 10-13%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same-day moves off TMX bars around Richelieu's intraday releases: Q2 FY26 EPS 0.42 vs 0.47 (miss of about 11%) went -8.91% on 2026-07-09; Q1 FY26 0.26 vs 0.30 went -4.22% on 2026-04-09; Q4 FY25 in line went -1.41% (+2.03% over two days); Q3 FY25 beat of +4.9% went +4.51% (+8.23% over two days) on 2025-10-09. EPS surprises have moved this stock roughly 0.4-0.9x.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a margin-driven miss, the two remaining analysts would carry about 0.44-0.45 rather than 0.46-0.48, and the last two misses would not have produced -8.9% and -4.2% same-day moves. A repeat miss has been treated as news each time. Against that, the trim from 0.51 to 0.48 in the last week and the stock's 11.5% YTD decline show the expectation is partly moving down already, so this finding is sized well below the history.
findings.independence: The bar comes from https://wealthawesome.com/will-richelieu-hardware-ltd-rch-beat-earnings-estimates-in-its-next-report-10062026-earnings (EPS history: 3 misses in 4). The Q1 margin-dilution quantification ('about 0.2') comes from a different document, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/richelieu-hardware-q1-earnings-call-163418387.html. The margin trend in finding 2 rests on the same disclosures, so these two findings share a basis.

findings.finding: The full-year aim of an EBITDA margin 'close to 11%' (CFO, Q2 call) implies about 11.9% in H2, given 10.0% in H1 on C$995.6M of sales, against 11.5% in H2 FY25 with tariff dilution still running. The CFO already hedged it ('we would need a bit more rigor in the market'), and the Q3 call at 10:00 ET on 8 October is likely to walk it down to roughly 10.5-10.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Richelieu gives no formal numeric guidance; margin commentary is the guide. The Q2 call where the 11% was hedged coincided with the -8.91% day (2026-07-09), and both analysts cut their targets on 2026-07-13. That move cannot be split between the EPS miss and the margin commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Both analysts still sit at 0.46-0.48 for Q3, which is consistent with modelling the H2 margin step-up. If they had abandoned it, Q3 EPS estimates would sit at or below the year-ago 0.43-0.45. The hedge was public, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: This shares its margin basis with finding 1, and the ~11% target is also stated in the Q1 call summary (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/richelieu-hardware-q1-earnings-call-163418387.html). The H1 figures come from the Q2 release (https://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/July2026/09/c6050.html).

findings.finding: USD/CAD averaged 1.4019 in June-August 2026 against 1.3720 in June-August 2025 (Bank of Canada daily series), a +2.2% translation tailwind on the roughly 45% of sales made in the US. That is worth about +1.0pt of reported growth and reverses the -1.1pt FX drag in Q2 (average rate 1.373 vs 1.407).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has been a disclosed swing factor: Q1 FY26 EBITDA would have been +5.6% excluding FX against +1.9% reported, and that quarter went -4.22%. No clean episode isolates FX.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of it probably is priced: consensus revenue of C$532.8-538.7M already matches a build that includes the FX tailwind. What may not be priced is the translation of US EBITDA into EPS if analysts modelled margin on the Q2 FX run-rate. It is sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms the size of the FX sensitivity (constant-currency +5.0% vs +3.9% reported): https://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/July2026/09/c6050.html

findings.finding: MasterBrand, the largest US cabinet maker and now owner of American Woodmark, reported a mid- to high-single-digit decline in the US cabinet market in its Q2 2026 (April-June) and forecasts a mid-single-digit decline in its 2026 addressable market. US cabinet manufacturers are Richelieu's core US customer base, and Richelieu's US manufacturers' internal growth was only +3.1% in Q2, partly from price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US manufacturers' line went from +7.3% internal in Q3 FY25 (tariff pricing; stock +4.51%) to +3.1% in Q2 FY26 (stock -8.91%). The deceleration has coincided with the weaker reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a counterparty print from after Richelieu last reported, with the weakest volume read in the group (legacy units -$47.9M). It is still a proxy: Richelieu's US specialty-closet business was growing 15-20% in June (Q2 call), so the transmission is uncertain and the finding is sized small.
findings.independence: The CEO's June commentary on the Q2 call ('we don't think that the months to come in the near future will help us') points the same way: https://www.webull.com/news/15219101599015936

findings.finding: Home Depot said Canada out-comped the company in its fiscal Q2 (May to 2 August 2026), with positive transactions and units, after a negative Q1. Canada is about 55% of Richelieu's sales, and its Canadian retailers' line was already +8.1% internal in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Canada grew +5.5% in Q2 FY26 (3.8% internal) and Quebec was up more than 10% in June, but the stock fell 8.91% on margin anyway. Canadian top-line strength has not carried the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a retail read-through on the smaller channel: retailers are about C$45M of Richelieu's C$291M in Canada. The manufacturers' channel, where Ontario is flat, dominates. It is small and probably partly in a consensus that already assumes Canadian growth.
findings.independence: The CEO's June commentary (Quebec +10%, Western Canada +5%) comes from a different document: https://www.webull.com/news/15219101599015936

findings.finding: On 2026-09-02 Richelieu bought Penrod's hardware division (about US$70M of annual sales, roughly 4.6% of group sales, US door hardware). It closed after the quarter, so it is outside the Q3 figures, but terms, financing and first-year contribution are likely to be given on the release or call. The Q3 balance sheet and call will also show the funding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement on 2026-09-02 after the close was met with +2.47% on 2026-09-03 (34.45 to 35.30 on TMX bars). Acquisition-heavy releases have had mixed reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is priced. The undisclosed price and terms are not, and Richelieu ran with net cash of C$12.4M in August 2025, so a modestly debt-funded deal does not change the balance-sheet story. That makes this a small, two-sided item.
findings.independence: The Drummondville expansion release (https://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/September2026/03/c2251.html) shows continued investment. It is the same company voice, not independent.

findings.finding: IEEPA duties were struck down on 2026-02-20 (Learning Resources v. Trump), and CBP's CAPE refund module has been processing claims since 2026-04-20 (Phase 2 from 2026-06-29). Richelieu imports into the US through 73 US distribution centres and passed tariffs through to customers in dollars, so any refund it books as importer of record would be a windfall in a quarter. Neither the Q2 release nor the Q2 call mentions a refund, so whether one is booked in Q3 is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on this name. A below-operating-income one-off with no path to the guide is sized at a fraction of operating-profit dollars.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither analyst's estimate is visibly built for a refund; consensus moved down, not up. The company has never quantified its IEEPA duty base (the CEO has said only that less than 20% of US products come from China), so nobody can model it. It is an inference about the company, which is why it is sized at 0.2.
findings.independence: MasterBrand said in its Q2 2026 release that tariff mitigation and refunds offset much of the burden, a peer booking refunds: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001941365/000194136526000070/q22026earningspressrelease.htm

outside_window.finding: The Drummondville distribution centre expansion (more than C$15M, from 40k to 180k sq ft) becomes operational in spring 2027. It is capex inside the C$18-20M guide and has no window effect.
